headline: America's Largest Land Wind Farm Now Powers the Southwest
meta_description: New Mexico's massive wind farm with 916 turbines generates 3.5 GW of clean electricity, transmitted across 550 miles to Arizona.
summary_short: America's biggest land-based wind farm is now operating in New Mexico, harnessing clean power from 916 turbines to serve the Southwest.
body:
America's largest land-based wind farm is now operating in New Mexico. The facility generates 3.5 gigawatts of clean electricity—enough to power hundreds of thousands of homes.

The scale of the project reflects years of renewable energy investment in the region. With 916 turbines working across the landscape, the farm represents one of the most significant steps yet toward displacing fossil fuels in the American energy grid.

The power doesn't stay in New Mexico. A 550-mile transmission line carries the wind energy across state lines to Arizona and California, extending the reach of this clean resource far beyond the farm's borders. This infrastructure underscores how renewable energy increasingly connects regions, allowing wind-rich areas to support electricity demand across the broader Southwest.
quick_facts: 916 turbines operating at New Mexico wind farm
550-mile transmission line to Arizona and California
